target_customer: Hotels first, then retail, restaurants and airlines that wanted point-of-sale customer feedback
problem: Online surveys get tiny response rates (about 2 percent per the launch coverage), so businesses learn little about service quality in real time.
business_model: B2B SaaS monthly subscription per iPad, with a preconfigured iPad and stand supplied

founders.name: Merrill Lutsky
education: Harvard (underclassman when the project began, per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him later as co-founder of Graphite. Technical status not stated in sources opened.

founders.name: Erik Schluntz
education: Harvard (underclassman when the project began, per TechCrunch)

technical_complexity.rationale: An iPad survey app with a web dashboard and email alerts was standard engineering for two Harvard students; the early prototype was rebuilt from PHP to Django per a Hack Harvard account seen in search.

defensibility.rationale: Survey software on a tablet was easy to copy; the launch article cites only response rate gains and about 50 standard question sets as differentiation.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A single database (Dealroom) says Revinate acquired it in July 2013, and Revinate later sold an iPad On-Site Surveys product, though no source ties the two together.

market_need_then: Launch coverage reports about 64 testers, of which roughly 20 to 25 converted to paid, and response rates near 30 percent versus about 2 percent for ordinary online surveys.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from PollVaultr per CB Insights and TechCrunch; no source explains the choice of Posmetrics.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; only launch coverage in March 2013.

pivots.from: PollVaultr point-of-sale survey system pitched to Harvard Square shops

outcome_analysis: Posmetrics launched in March 2013 after the YC Winter 2013 batch with early paying testers and strong survey response rates, but the product was easy to copy and the team was two students. A single database says Revinate acquired the company in July 2013, which fits the Inactive status and suggests a quick soft landing rather than an independent path. No deal terms are public, so the real driver is unconfirmed.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503 (likely dead). Acquisition by Revinate and the $80K seed rest on single databases (Dealroom, CB Insights); no press release found. TechCrunch (2013-03) says under $500K outside funding including YC, which does not match CB's $80K, so funding is partial. Competitor list is empty because the launch article names none and a dated search found none. Tool problem: CB Insights fetch blocked, not worked around. Directory status is Inactive while exit.type is acquisition: the company stopped operating independently after the reported acquisition or acquihire, so the conflict is explained.
